description: Indulge in the rich and creamy flavors of authentic Butter Chicken, a cherished Indian delicacy known as Murgh Makhani. This classic recipe features tender chicken pieces simmered in a luscious tomato-based gravy, enriched with butter and cream. Perfect for a hearty family meal, it promises a truly satisfying culinary experience.

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 30 min

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, a pinch of salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to coat the chicken thoroughly. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or for best results, 2-4 hours.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of cooking oil and 1 tablespoon of butter in a large heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary, to avoid overcrowding. Cook until the chicken is lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until it becomes soft and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, cloves, and bay leaf, and sauté for another minute until aromatic.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Add the tomato puree, remaining 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, and a pinch of salt to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the oil to separate from the gravy. Stir in the soaked cashews and 1/2 cup of water. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook for another 5 minutes.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain for Smoothness
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf and cinnamon stick from the gravy mixture. Let the mixture cool slightly, then carefully transfer it to a blender. Blend until it forms a completely smooth puree. For an exceptionally silky and restaurant-style gravy, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pan, pressing down on the solids to extract all the liquid.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Stir in the crushed kasoori methi, sugar, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon garam masala. Add the previously cooked chicken pieces to the gravy. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter. Heat through gently for 2-3 minutes, without bringing to a vigorous boil, to prevent the cream from splitting. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.

tips: For a deeper, smoky flavor, you can grill or pan-fry the marinated chicken until slightly charred before adding it to the gravy. This mimics the traditional tandoor cooking method.
Soaking cashews for at least 30 minutes before blending is crucial for achieving a super smooth and rich gravy texture, free from any graininess.

Always add the heavy cream and the final portion of butter at the very end of cooking. Heat gently without boiling vigorously to maintain the gravy's velvety consistency and prevent it from splitting.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in its authentic Indian name as Murgh Makhani, stands as a crowning jewel of Indian cuisine. This globally celebrated dish captivates palates with its creamy, rich, and subtly sweet-tangy tomato-based sauce, enveloping succulent pieces of marinated chicken. It’s a testament to the magic that happens when simple ingredients are combined with expert technique and a touch of culinary love. Whether you’re a seasoned cook or new to Indian cooking, mastering Murgh Makhani promises a deeply satisfying culinary experience that brings the warmth and spice of India right to your dining table.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

At its heart, Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a classic Indian curry originating from Delhi in the mid-20th century. The name itself, "Murgh Makhani," literally translates to "chicken with butter," hinting at the luxurious richness that defines this dish. It features tender chicken pieces, traditionally marinated in yogurt and spices, then cooked in a velvety sauce made from tomatoes, butter, cream, and a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala, ginger, garlic, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). Unlike many other Indian curries, Butter Chicken is not overwhelmingly spicy; instead, it offers a harmonious balance of flavors – a slight tang from the tomatoes, a hint of sweetness, and a profound depth from the spices and richness of the dairy. Its iconic orange-red hue and irresistible aroma have made it a favorite across continents.

## Ingredients for Classic Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a careful selection of fresh ingredients to achieve that signature taste and texture.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color without excessive heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   400g canned crushed tomatoes or tomato puree
*   1/4 cup cashews or blanched almonds (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes) for richness and thickening
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1 tablespoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1 teaspoon sugar (optional, to balance tanginess)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro for garnish

The yogurt in the marinade tenderizes the chicken, while the spices infuse it with flavor. For the sauce, tomatoes form the tangy base, butter and cream provide the luxurious mouthfeel, and cashews contribute a subtle nuttiness and help create that silky smooth consistency. Kasoori methi is a non-negotiable ingredient, lending an earthy, slightly bitter, and uniquely aromatic note that is characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani.

## How to Make Butter Chicken: Step-by-Step Guide

Making this beloved Butter Chicken dish involves a few key stages, each contributing to the final masterpiece.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to deepen and the chicken to tenderize.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F) or a grill pan on medium-high heat. Spread the marinated chicken in a single layer on a baking sheet or grill the pieces until lightly charred and cooked through. This step adds a smoky depth to the chicken. Set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Makhani Sauce Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the butter and oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Add Spices and Tomatoes:** Reduce the heat to low, then add the red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, and garam masala. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, to bloom the spices. Immediately pour in the crushed tomatoes or tomato puree. Add the soaked cashews/almonds and water/broth. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down.
5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the hot sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until perfectly smooth and creamy. For an extra silky texture, you can strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot, pressing down on any solids.
6.  **Finish the Butter Chicken:** Return the smooth sauce to the pot over low heat. Stir in the heavy cream, crushed kasoori methi, and sugar (if using). Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Taste and adjust salt or sweetness as needed.

## Expert Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few insider tricks:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't rush the marination process. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will become. Overnight marination in the refrigerator yields the best results.
*   **Sear or Grill the Chicken:** While you can simply cook the chicken in the sauce, searing or grilling it beforehand adds a crucial layer of smoky flavor and texture that elevates the dish significantly.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** The signature silky texture of Murgh Makhani comes from thoroughly blending the sauce. Take your time with this step, ensuring there are no grainy bits from the onions or cashews. A high-speed blender is ideal.
*   **Don't Skip Kasoori Methi:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are non-negotiable for authentic flavor. Gently crush them between your palms before adding to release their aromatic oils.
*   **Balance Sweetness and Tang:** Depending on the sweetness of your tomatoes, you might need to adjust the sugar. The goal is a balanced flavor profile, not overly sweet. A pinch of sugar often helps to cut through the acidity of the tomatoes and enhance the overall taste.
*   **Use Quality Butter and Cream:** Since butter and cream are star ingredients, using good quality dairy products will make a noticeable difference in the final richness and flavor of your Butter Chicken.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments. For a truly authentic Indian dining experience, serve your Murgh Makhani hot, garnished with a swirl of fresh cream and a sprinkle of chopped fresh cilantro.

*   **Naan Bread:** The soft, chewy texture of naan is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly delightful choices.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Fragrant basmati rice, either plain or as Jeera Rice (rice flavored with cumin seeds), provides a wonderful contrast and absorbs the curry’s flavors beautifully.
*   **Roti or Chapati:** For a lighter option, whole wheat Indian flatbreads like roti or chapati are excellent accompaniments.
*   **Raita:** A cooling side of cucumber raita (yogurt with grated cucumber and mild spices) can offer a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry.
*   **Simple Salad:** A fresh, crisp green salad can also provide a nice balance to the hearty nature of the Butter Chicken.

## Butter Chicken Variations & FAQs

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is a beloved standard, its popularity has inspired several delicious variations and common questions.

**Variations:**
*   **Paneer Makhani:** A popular vegetarian alternative where cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese) replace the chicken, offering a similar creamy, flavorful experience.
*   **Shrimp Makhani:** For seafood lovers, shrimp can be marinated and cooked in the same rich sauce.
*   **Vegan Makhani:** Coconut milk and pureed cashews can replace dairy cream and butter, and plant-based protein like tofu or chickpeas can be used instead of chicken for a delicious vegan version.

**FAQs:**
*   **Is Butter Chicken spicy?** Traditionally, Butter Chicken is mild, with its spice level adjusted more for aroma and flavor than heat. However, you can easily increase the amount of red chili powder or add a fresh green chili for more kick.
*   **Can I make it ahead of time?** Absolutely! Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
*   **Can I freeze Butter Chicken?** Yes, it freezes very well. Once cooled, transfer it to freezer-safe containers and freeze for up to 2-3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat gently on the stovetop.
*   **What kind of tomatoes should I use?** High-quality canned crushed tomatoes or tomato puree work best for consistency and flavor, especially if fresh tomatoes are not perfectly ripe.

Butter Chicken is more than just a dish; it's a culinary journey. Its global appeal is a testament to its perfectly balanced flavors and comforting texture. Whether you're making it for a special occasion or a cozy weeknight meal, this classic Murgh Makhani recipe is sure to impress and satisfy. So roll up your sleeves, gather your ingredients, and prepare to create a truly unforgettable Indian feast right in your own kitchen.
